correctness.rationale: The fibre lemma is exact: after reducing z to (alpha,1-alpha), explicit witnesses attain the two branches and a complete sign/crossing split gives matching upper bounds. For a one-coordinate outer point every unit y decomposes into fibre mass a and complementary p-mass 1-a^p, so the optimization is exactly one scalar function. Its first branch is bounded by 2 and its second branch is increasing, leaving only 2 and [2(1-alpha)]^p. For arbitrary x, infinitude of Gamma provides coordinates of arbitrarily small norm, and a fresh-coordinate witness gives the uniform lower bound 2^(1/p). A balanced one-coordinate fibre realizes equality.
risks: The pointwise classification is only for one-coordinate base points.
The exact rational checker is supplementary to the analytic continuum proof.

value.rationale: The finding gives a complete pointwise profile on every one-coordinate diamond fibre and identifies the exact competition between fresh outer coordinates and in-fibre antipodal geometry. The global index follows sharply with an attained balanced minimizer. For p>2 the value is strictly separated from the known Hilbert-fibre value sqrt(2), giving a concrete fibre-sensitivity phenomenon for a canonical direct-sum construction. This is a structural benchmark beyond the qualitative LOH criterion.
risks: The theorem is a two-dimensional fibre model rather than a classification for all polyhedral fibres.
Higher-dimensional ell_1 fibres may involve a more complicated partition optimization.
